sections.heading: Function
paragraphs: TET3 is responsible for converting 5-methylcytosine (5mC) to 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC), which is responsible for initiating active DNA demethylation [Ketchum et al., 2024].

paragraphs.text: Our cohort analysis discovers the case(s) in rare frequency that TET3 is disturbed as shown here.

sections.heading: Literature
paragraphs: When TET3 is compromised, downstream signaling required for neural crest cell differentiation and pharyngeal cartilage formation is impaired, which can lead to craniofacial malformations like cleft lip and palate [Chen et al., 2023, Wang et al., 2024].

paragraphs.text: Our analysis discovers the case(s) in rare frequency that demonstrates the oligogenic interaction involving TET3.
paragraphs.suffix: to see the co-occurring SVs that are appearing with TET3 in our curated palatogenesis pathway diagram. It shows the involvement of developmental enhancers via the TET-SNAIL4-BMP axis.

sections.heading: EMT
paragraphs: It is related to EMT, indirectly but convincingly. TET proteins are frequently found upstream of EMT programs because EMT requires large-scale epigenetic reprogramming. TET-mediated DNA demethylation can regulate expression of genes involved in: cell fate transitions, epithelial identity, migration, differentiation. It may not be an EMT transcription factor, but it can be labelled as EMT-enabling epigenetic regulator.
